subject: Retention matrix, regional store fallbacks & migration Q&A
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinServe Legal <legal@finserve.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention needs and regional controls

Thanks Marissa — quick context from our side. We have two principal constraints: 1) Certain payment-ledger records must remain in US-only storage for 7 years, immutable; 2) Session logs for some EU customers must be deletable within 90 days on request. We want an approach that avoids per-tenant manual migrations when a customer changes region or compliance classification. Can you share options?

—Sara
Product Ops, FinServe
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@finserve.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention needs and regional controls

Sara — thanks for the clarity. High level options we support and trade-offs: 

• Per-tenant binding (current Recommended): tenant metadata pins region + retention profile. Simplifies enforcement but requires migration when tenant requests region change (we can do live rehydrate+copy or background swap).
• Multi-zone object tagging: each object stores residency tag and TTL; routing layer enforces write/read locality and delete hooks. More flexible but higher storage and complexity for garbage collection.
• Hybrid: sensitive classes (ledgers) pinned to a single regional store; ephemeral logs use location-agnostic stores with shorter TTLs.

I've attached a retention matrix draft and a fallback routing diagram. Karthik — are there engineering constraints I should call out for live migration? Lauren/Hannah — anything from legal/sales perspective we should flag for FinServe?

Best,
Marissa 
Enterprise Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@finserve.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T10:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention needs and regional controls

Marissa/Sara — quick tech notes on migration modes: 

1) Live mirror + cutover: replicate objects to target region, switch metadata pointer. Pros: minimal downtime (read-only window for final switchover). Cons: double write cost during replication window; must ensure KMS key availability in target region.

2) Tiered export/import: export immutable classes via snapshot, import to new region, update pointers. Pros: cheaper for very large datasets; Cons: longer lead time and manual verification.

3) Policy-based on-read relocation (lazy migration): first read triggers copy to target, then delete source after verification. Pros: avoids copying cold data; Cons: complexity and potential for cross-region reads during transition.

Engineering gotchas for FinServe-specific ask: 
• Immutable ledger records require HSM-backed KEKs per region (we cannot simply copy encrypted blobs without key escrow arrangement).
• Deletion API must expose per-object purge and time-windowed retention hold (for legal holds).
• Rollout: we can prototype tenant-pin + hybrid storage in 6 weeks (P0 work) and follow with lazy-migration fallback in next quarter.

—Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@finserve.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-23T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention needs and regional controls

Sara — legal flags and customer-facing considerations: 

• We should offer a clear SLA for migration duration and a pricing note for cross-region replication costs.
• For immutable financial ledgers we recommend explicit attestation language in the contract about regional KMS keys and any required export approvals.
• Helpdesk flow: if a customer requests region change, open a migration ticket with estimated ETA and a schedule for validation.

I've attached a short summary PDF for FinServe that explains options in customer-friendly language. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk FinServe through trade-offs.

—Lauren
Head of Compliance & Policy, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Retention needs and regional controls

Sara — following up with next steps we propose: 

1) Pilot plan: enable tenant-pin + hybrid storage for a single FinServe sandbox tenant (no ledger migration), timeframe: 6 weeks.
2) Ledger migration runbook: Karthik to draft HSM/KMS checklist and migration playbook (targeted delivery in 3 weeks).
3) Pricing addendum: Lauren will propose an export/replication surcharge and a certified attestation clause.

Can you confirm a 30-minute walkthrough next week (dates: July 28/29 preferred)? If you agree, we'll attach the pilot SOW and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a scoped pilot.

Best,
Marissa
